speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Manpower what plans are in place to help gig economy workers access group medical insurance as well as save for retirement and home ownership.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SEPs' concerns were more about their loss of income when they fall sick for prolonged periods.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The National Instructors and Coaches Association also offers discounted PML insurance for their members.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We encourage more service-buyers and associations to support their SEPs with such insurance coverage.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Like regular employees, SEPs can save for home ownership and retirement through the Central Provident Fund (CPF) system.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can do so by making voluntary CPF contributions and benefit from the higher-than-market interest rates.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Lower-income SEPs receive additional support through the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: WIS encourages lower-income workers to stay employed and strengthen their retirement adequacy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I wonder if the Ministry will consider studying a Government-led mandatory medical benefit system for the self-employed that will cover things like paid medical leave as well as co-payments for outpatient care.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: That is because it might be more efficient than relying on private provision of these systems because there are issues with adverse selection and also gaps in coverage outside the sectors that the Ministry has worked on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The first is that, if you look at our MediShield Life system, it already covers everyone, including the SEPs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, there is one layer of protection that an SEP will already have.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The second is that we are very mindful that in some instances, what is considered a self-employment arrangement may, in fact, be a mis-classification.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Then, in those instances, the right thing to do is to rectify or regularise that arrangement so that the employer rightly provides for the individual in terms of medical benefits.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The third is really people whose nature of work involves them contracting with multiple service buyers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Under those circumstances, if we were to say that each one of those service buyers would be responsible for some part of the medical provision, I think there are complications in terms of implementation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I accept the fact that, indeed, on a system basis, it may be more efficient to get the individual covered but that is really the whole purpose of MediShield Life to begin with.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The most fundamental worry that we all have with SEPs is their savings for retirement and, to a large extent, also towards housing.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, would the Minister consider launching a matched retirement savings scheme, a scheme where perhaps the Government can contribute when they put some money in to save towards housing needs and also their retirement?
